summary.text: Identity.md’s project runs a contract-backed AI-agent network that builds websites, software and research for customers.
Customers submit work through its explorer, while seat holders run worker agents on their own machines.
The wider project includes customer and worker apps, token launches, community coins and an IMD trading pool.
A standard Ethereum job costs 0.5 IMD, and the API currently reports 8,450 paid orders.
The Intake contract takes payments that fund the network treasury; token and pool trades connect launches to staking and burns, the project says.
The docs describe work checked by other agents, while seat holders provide their own computers and AI subscriptions.
The deployer wallet owns the token and Intake; Blockscout code gives it setting controls, but who controls that wallet is unknown.

lines.text: The docs say job payments go to the treasury that pays to run the network.
lines.quote: Every payment goes to the IMD treasury, which pays to run the network.

lines.text: The docs allocate 8% of each launched token to seats online when the launch is admitted.
lines.quote: 8% of every token the swarm launches goes to the seats online when it is admitted.

lines.text: The docs allocate another 2% of a launched token to wallets with accepted work on that launch.
lines.quote: Another 2% goes to the wallets with accepted work on that launch.

lines.text: The API docs say text outputs receive structural checks.
lines.quote: For a text output it is the structure alone.

lines.text: The API docs say contract checks build and test the code.
lines.quote: forge build and forge test

lines.text: @surfcoderepeat says he developed the first version alone.
lines.quote: as developed this alone

lines.text: @surfcoderepeat says new IMD launches can pair their tokens with imdUSD.
lines.quote: You can now pair new tokens with imdUSD (@imdusd)

lines.text: The public API lists imdUSD as an Ethereum token launch pairing.
lines.quote: "pairWith":"imdusd"

lines.text: The current IMD docs and public API limit a single goal to 50 agents at a time.
lines.quote: 50 agents at a time

lines.text: The docs date the Fren Pet predecessor launch to August 2023.
lines.quote: Aug 2023 Fren Pet launches on Base as $FP.

lines.text: The docs date the free mint of the 2,000 seat NFTs to May 2026.
lines.quote: May 2026 identity.md mints. 2,000 NFTs, free, one per wallet.

lines.text: IMD’s docs list token addresses on Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain.
lines.quote: Split across Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain, bridged one for one.

lines.text: Taylor McKnight lists @taylor_ on his personal site.
lines.quote: Taylor McKnight

lines.text: Bankless reports that the agent network opened to seat holders on September 20, 2026.
lines.quote: The agent network opened to NFT holders on September 20th

lines.quote: official communication is published as on-chain messages from this address

lines.text: Bankless reports that a seat authorizes one active device.
lines.quote: A single NFT authorizes one active device, and holders pay for the compute.

lines.text: Blockscout’s published token code says the owner can change the name and symbol.
lines.quote: Updates both name and symbol of the token in a single transaction. Only callable by the owner.

lines.text: Blockscout’s published payment contract code gives the owner control over prices, payout, writer and signer.
lines.quote: function setPayTo(address to) external onlyOwner

lines.text: IMD says its payment contract forwards each job payment to the configured payee in the same call.
lines.quote: Every Intake payment is forwarded here in the same call.

lines.text: POOL4 says users deposit IMD in its vault and receive sIMD shares.
lines.quote: Stake IMD, get sIMD

lines.text: POOL4 says its reward dripper sends 4.5% of the IMD removed from the pool to the staking vault.
lines.quote: 4.5% of every batch the market retires streams into the vault

lines.text: POOL4 says 6% of the removed IMD is reserved for the lead agent’s computing capacity.
lines.quote: 6 into the bonding reserve for the lead orchestrator

lines.text: POOL4 says 4.5% of the removed IMD is reserved for computing nodes run by seat holders.
lines.quote: 4.5 reserved for NFT inference nodes

lines.text: POOL4 says any caller can pay the bridge fee to send a batch of burn-bound IMD to Base.
lines.quote: Anyone can pay the LayerZero fee to bridge a batch to Base

lines.text: POOL4 says ETH recovered when its pool removes excess IMD goes back to the pool as a standing buy order.
lines.quote: ETH recovered from the trim becomes a standing bid under the market.

lines.text: POOL4 says the pool hook trims excess IMD after sales.
lines.quote: A hook on that pool trims excess IMD after sells.

lines.text: IMD says its bridge locks the original token on Base and mints matching IMD on Ethereum and Robinhood Chain.
lines.quote: It is locked in the bridge adapter on Base and minted against that lock on Ethereum and Robinhood

lines.text: IMD says each trade of a Community Coin burns part of its paired IMD.
lines.quote: Community coins are tokens launched against IMD, and every trade of one burns IMD too.

lines.text: Blockscout’s published trading hook source says anyone can send accrued Community Coins burn fees to the burn executor.
lines.quote: Send all accrued burn-fee IMD to the burn executor. Anyone can call.

lines.text: IMD’s API reference says the current launch factories allocate 1% of each trade to the paying wallet.
lines.quote: 1% to the paying wallet

lines.text: IMD’s API reference says the current launch factories allocate 0.25% of each trade to the network.
lines.quote: 0.25% to the network

lines.text: IMD’s API reference says anyone can trigger distribution of launch trading fees.
lines.quote: Anyone can call the distribution.

lines.text: IMD’s API reference says workers claim the shares of launched tokens through a contract that checks proofs of eligibility.
lines.quote: Claimed from the launch's Merkle distributor

lines.text: IMD’s API reference says the Ethereum work receipt records a hash of the work and feedback for the agents.
lines.quote: The transaction records the hash of the work document and gives each agent its feedback on the reputation registry.

lines.text: IMD’s API reference says Sepolia uses imdTEST to pay for test jobs.
lines.quote: Sepolia sells in imdTEST

lines.text: IMD’s API reference says it stopped accepting its first Sepolia payment token on October 18, 2026.
lines.quote: is priced at 0 there since 2026-10-18, so a payment in it reverts.

lines.text: IMD’s API reference lists Uniswap v4 as the infrastructure for launch trading pools.
lines.quote: Where launch pools live.

lines.text: @taylor_ says ETH collected as launch fees on Ethereum and Robinhood Chain is used to buy IMD to burn.
lines.quote: Launch fees on Ethereum and Robinhood Chain now feed the burn: IMD is burned, ETH buys IMD to burn.

lines.text: @surfcoderepeat credits @yadfarms with developing imdUSD on top of IMD.
lines.quote: imdUSD is an agents backed stable coin developed by @yadfarms on top of IMD

lines.text: Built by IMD says the network builds apps.
lines.quote: IMD is a swarm in the sky that builds apps, sites, contracts, tokens and more.

lines.text: Blockscout’s verified Community Coins factory source names communitycoins.imd.fun as the factory’s site.
lines.quote: /// https://communitycoins.imd.fun

lines.text: Blockscout’s verified Community Coins factory source says anyone can launch a coin backed by IMD.
lines.quote: Permissionlessly launches coins backed by IMD.

lines.text: IMD’s docs say a customer can follow a job while it is being built.
lines.quote: Then watch the job get built.

lines.text: IMD offers a searchable database of a customer’s smart contract activity.
lines.quote: as a database you can query

lines.text: IMD charges 0.5 IMD for a research goal without additional deliverables.
lines.quote: Choose Research only to buy none and pay 0.5.

lines.text: IMD charges another 0.5 IMD per item a goal asks it to create.
lines.quote: 0.5 IMD, and 0.5 per thing it makes

lines.text: IMD links to the worker app’s source code in its Identity-md GitHub organization.
lines.quote: Identity-md/desktop

lines.text: IMD’s documentation refers to a team distinct from the seat holders who write community guides.
lines.quote: Written by seat holders, not by the IMD team.

lines.text: IMD offers a site for launching community tokens paired with IMD.
lines.quote: Community coins are tokens launched against IMD

lines.text: POOL4 operates an IMD trading pool on Ethereum.
lines.quote: IMD trades in a full-range ETH/IMD Uniswap v4 pool.

lines.text: @0xminion reported 3,989 paid network orders by October 12, 2026.
lines.quote: Paid orders stand at 3,989

lines.text: Onchain Atlas found a public IMD repository dating to August 15, 2026.
lines.quote: The earliest first-party public repository verified in this review dates to August 15, 2026

lines.text: Onchain Atlas reports that IMD’s service controls which jobs enter the network and how they are assigned.
lines.quote: the control plane admits jobs, assigns tasks, applies policy, coordinates verification, and publishes results

lines.text: The IMD API lists Ethereum, Base, Robinhood Chain and Sepolia for contract launches.
lines.quote: "evm_contracts"

lines.text: IMD says its deployer records work receipts on Ethereum when jobs end.
lines.quote: When a job ends, the deployer writes a receipt

lines.text: POOL4 says its swap fee stays in a separate ledger as protocol revenue.
lines.quote: The 1% fee is protocol revenue. It sits in its own ledger

lines.text: POOL4 says anyone can trigger releases of staking rewards from the reward buffer into the vault.
lines.quote: drip staking yield, and finish burns on Base. Anyone can run them.

lines.text: POOL4 says it tracks allocations for bonding and nodes onchain while those programs are being built.
lines.quote: Bonding and node allocations are tracked on-chain

lines.text: The Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain IMD bridge contracts name each other as peers, and the Base adapter names Fren Pet as its token.

differs.why: The API reference says the listed sources are unverified. The current Blockscout response for the listed main token marks its source verified.
The November 11 post says 100 simultaneous agents; current IMD documentation and API list 50 per goal. It is unclear whether the post described a separate mode.
The 276 hackathon agents could have been spread over several goals or rounds. The number active at the same time is unclear.
The repository counts seats while Taylor counts agents. How many issued seats were active at the time is unclear.

Trenchcoat reported no owner controls in its November 11 scan. The published token source describes owner-only name and symbol changes, and owner() returned the deployer at both ends of that date and on November 24.

open_questions: Can a contract, ENS record or deployer wallet verify the project’s social accounts?
Who controls the owner, treasury, signer and writer wallets, and which other contracts can each change?
What is the circulating supply across chains after excluding the Base backing locked in the bridge?
Why does the API reference describe all its listed source code as unverified while Blockscout verifies the main token?
Does the 100-agent description refer to another mode or an earlier goal limit?
Which deployments and launch contracts on Base are currently used in production?
What is the full cost of completing different types of work, including gas, subscriptions and launch funding?
What is the Base burn receiver address, and how much of the node and bonding reserves has been distributed?
How many independent customers pay for jobs, and how often do accepted results meet their requirements?
Who can issue or redeem imdUSD, and what assets or services back it?
notes: Sources read: imd.fun home, product docs and API docs; explorer launch page; Community Coins site; current health and capabilities APIs; the earlier sourced record and all listed panel-answer records. what_it_does: The current home page leads with hiring AI agents, while docs list the network products. how_it_works: Docs describe requests, agent work and checking; current public launch form is live. money: Docs and the live API both state 0.5 IMD for standard Ethereum jobs; the current API count is 8,450 paid orders. people: Existing cited reports identify the creator account, but sources read do not establish who operates the project today or who controls the deployer wallet. on_chain: Carried proofs describe token supply and contract settings; current contract settings were not re-read at a new block in this run. history: The carried record covers the Fren Pet predecessor and the later network launch. Inference: the Ethereum Intake contract is the main customer-facing contract because it accepts paid job requests. Uncertainty: whether the identified wallet is controlled by the named creator remains open.

how_it_works.text: Describe a job on the explorer and connect a wallet to pay.
Intake records a request and forwards its payment to the configured receiver; the docs say job payments fund the network treasury.
Agents build the requested result, and other agents review it before delivery.
A standard Ethereum job costs 0.5 IMD; work that creates extra items may cost more.
Seat holders run workers on their own machines and pay for their own AI plans.
The API currently reports 8,450 paid orders.

sentences.text: IMD pays for jobs, launches and oracle questions.
Whether holding IMD gives rights beyond its listed uses was not checked.
The docs provide a buy action for IMD.
The docs say 10 million were created in 2023, none since, and the supply only decreases.
The docs say pool and community coin trading move IMD to staking or burn destinations.
The Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain forms are connected as one bridged token.
The home token supply is on Base; some is held there to back bridged tokens.
Pool and community coin activity sends portions of IMD to staking or burn destinations, as the project describes.
The owner can change the token name and symbol.
Who could create or destroy IMD tokens was not checked.
Intake v2 accepts paid job requests.
Its owner can change prices, payout address, writer and signer.
A change to those settings could affect future payments and processing of requests.
